technical_and_design_decisions: Use Spring Data Gemfire as the foundational client library for Gemfire interactions, since it provides idiomatic Spring abstractions and lifecycle management over the native Gemfire Java client.

Implement the Gemfire binder against the Spring Cloud Stream Binder SPI v1.x, following the producer/consumer model already used by Kafka and RabbitMQ binders, with one Gemfire region per logical channel.

Model the Gemfire SPI for Spring Cloud Data Flow as a pluggable TaskLauncher/StreamDeployer abstraction, with a Gemfire-backed implementation that uses Gemfire function execution and CQ to coordinate stream lifecycle and module orchestration across nodes.

Model the stream repository (U3) on top of Gemfire REPLICATE regions (one per stream definition) to support high-availability read access and consistency for stream definitions; stream deployment state is stored in a separate PARTITION region.

Model the module registry (U4) as a single PARTITION region keyed by module coordinate (group:artifact:version) holding registration metadata (URL, type, checksum), with server-side functions to query and resolve modules.

Implement the tap feature (U7) as a runtime-only fork by subscribing an additional Gemfire CQ client to the source region's events; this avoids duplicating data on producers and matches the 'without impacting the original stream' requirement.

Extend the Spring Cloud Data Flow DSL with a 'tap' keyword that produces a sub-stream definition; the DSL is parsed and translated to the same stream definition model, while the shell (U8) exposes a 'stream tap' command for ad-hoc forks.

Treat documentation activities (U5, U6) as reference documentation, not implementation: one reference page per topic with runnable example command(s) and an explanation of the underlying option semantics.
All binders/SPIs ship with a Spring Boot auto-configuration module using @ConfigurationProperties so users can configure Gemfire connection (locators, security, PDX) declaratively.
assumptions: A single experienced Java/Spring developer performs the work; estimates do not include management, code review, or coordination overhead.
A working local Gemfire cluster (or pulse/embedded) is available for development and testing; no environment provisioning work is included.
The Gemfire binder is a new module — there is no existing code to modify beyond configuring it as a child of spring-cloud-stream and spring-cloud-dataflow.
The tap feature (U7/U8) is implemented at the runtime/DSL layer only and does not require changes to existing module implementations (sources/processors/sinks).
Unit and integration tests are included inside each feature activity; a dedicated cross-cutting system-test activity is added for full end-to-end pipeline verification.
Java 17+ baseline is assumed (per Spring Framework 6.0 requirement) and Groovy/Kotlin interop is not specifically required by the user stories.
Documentation is produced in Asciidoc to match existing Spring Cloud project conventions and is sized accordingly.
No localization, marketing, or website work is included; only developer- and user-facing reference/usage documentation.
Performance/load testing is scoped as part of integration testing only; no dedicated benchmarking activity is added.

activities.activity_description: Define the overall module structure (binder module, SPI module, repository, registry, DSL/shell changes), design the Gemfire region/property model, draft interface contracts for the binder, SPI, repository and registry, and produce a short design note for each. Includes dependency selection (Spring Data Gemfire version) and skeleton pom.xml files.

Implement the Spring Cloud Stream Binder SPI for Gemfire: MessageChannelBinder subclass, GemfireMessageHandler (consumer), GemfireMessageProducer (producer), GemfireClientFactory, configuration metadata, error handling and dead-letter handling. Includes unit tests for serialization, partition routing, and ack semantics, and integration tests against an embedded Gemfire server.

activities.activity_name: Implement Gemfire SPI for Spring Cloud Data Flow (U2)
activities.activity_description: Define the SPI interfaces (StreamOrchestrator, ModuleOrchestrator) and provide a Gemfire-backed implementation that uses function execution and continuous queries to coordinate stream and module deployment across a Gemfire cluster. Includes a Gemfire SPI autoconfiguration module and integration tests orchestrating a 3-module sample stream.

Implement StreamRepository against Gemfire: CRUD for stream definitions, indexing by name/label, and pagination. Includes conversion between the internal StreamDefinition model and the persisted representation, optimistic concurrency control, and tests covering create/read/update/delete and concurrent updates.

Implement ModuleRegistry on top of a Gemfire region: register, unregister, query-by-coordinate, and resolve modules for a stream. Include checksum verification hooks and tests covering registration, lookup, version conflict and unregistration.

activities.activity_name: Implement tap on the primary pipeline (U7)
activities.activity_description: Add runtime support to attach an additional subscriber (CQ-based) to a running stream so the same events are consumed in parallel without affecting the original consumer. Includes lifecycle management (attach/detach tap), back-pressure consideration, and tests covering tap attach, data fidelity, and detach.

activities.activity_name: Add tap support to DSL and Shell (U8)
activities.activity_description: Extend the Spring Cloud Data Flow DSL grammar to allow a 'tap' construct producing a sub-stream, and add a 'stream tap' command in the interactive shell that creates a tap destination stream. Includes parser tests, shell command tests, and an end-to-end test that creates a tap from the shell and verifies the forked data flow.

Write the deployment manifest reference page explaining partition count, partition selector expressions, and how partition keys affect stream parallelism. Include a complete manifest example and screenshots/diagrams of partitioned execution.

Write the 'direct binding' reference page with the launcher jar command-line example from U6, explanation of --modules, --args and --aggregate flags, and a worked end-to-end example (time-source -> filter -> filter -> sink) that the user can run verbatim.

Add Spring Boot auto-configuration for all new modules (binder, SPI, repository, registry, tap runtime), @ConfigurationProperties classes, conditional beans, and assemble the final starter module that pulls them together. Includes sample application.yml and packaging of executable jars.

Build an end-to-end test suite that starts a Gemfire locator/server, registers modules, deploys a partitioned stream, taps it, and verifies both primary and tapped outputs. Includes test profiles, embedded Gemfire lifecycle, and CI-friendly configuration.

activities.activity_name: User guide, getting-started and release notes
activities.activity_description: Write a getting-started section, configuration guide, troubleshooting page, and release notes covering the new binder, SPI, repository, registry, and tap features. Update the table of contents and cross-link to the reference pages produced in A8 and A9.
